narrative.overview: ArcWriter is a calm, local-first writing desk rather than an AI control room. Its warm paper ground keeps the manuscript and the author in charge; cool violet-grey neutrals recede into navigation, controls and operational detail. A restrained plum accent marks the few places where a user can act, commit or understand current selection. The system has the density of a professional desktop tool, but it earns density through hierarchy and progressive disclosure.
keyCharacteristics: Warm reading surfaces, cool operational surfaces and one controlled plum accent.
Chinese-first desktop typography, with a dedicated Songti manuscript voice.
Fine 1px dividers and tonal changes establish structure before shadows do.
Inline confirmation and right-side drawers preserve context instead of interrupting it.
Compact controls, 1024px minimum desktop layout and a collapsed navigation treatment for narrow windows.

rules.name: The One Plum Rule
rules.body: Plum is an action and selection signal. Keep it below roughly one tenth of a normal workspace surface, so the next meaningful action remains immediately legible.

rules.name: The Status Must Speak Rule
rules.body: Success, warning and error always appear with explicit Chinese status copy and, where space permits, an icon. Colour is reinforcement, never the only carrier of meaning.

rules.name: The Manuscript Has the Last Word Rule
rules.body: In an active editor, manuscript text is visually larger, more spacious and more central than every navigation or AI control around it.

rules.name: The Paper Stack Rule
rules.body: If a surface can be separated by paper, stone or a fine rule, do that. Add a shadow only when the surface physically overlays another working plane.

dos: Do keep the main workspace on Warm Paper and support rails or secondary panels on Violet Stone.
Do show AI context, destination, overwrite scope, failure reason and recovery action near the operation that needs them.
Do use progressive disclosure: message preview first, right-side review drawer second, a modal only when the work genuinely cannot remain in context.
donts: Don't turn ArcWriter into a generic SaaS dashboard, with hero metrics, equal-weight card grids or a control-room visual hierarchy.
Don't use decorative glassmorphism, large high-saturation blue fields or purple gradients.
Don't make the interface resemble a code IDE.
Don't let three columns compete at equal visual weight.
Don't use a coloured left or right card stripe, gradient text, decorative blur or shadow stacks to manufacture hierarchy.
Don't hide what AI read, where a result will write or what an overwrite replaces.
